Subject: Sudden p95/p99 regressions on our 16k workflows (production)

Hi Soojin,

We're seeing significant latency regressions since Friday across our hosted calls that use the 16k window — p95 has jumped from ~420ms to ~1.3s and p99 is frequently >3s. This is hitting our customer-facing document summarization route and causing timeouts in our ingestion pipeline. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (model: rdx-encoder-16k-v2).

Attached is a small sample of request IDs and repro traces (lexicon_error_samples.txt). We're on a production schedule this week — can you triage urgently? Our SRE would like to know whether this is a runtime regression, a model rollout, or a capacity issue.

Thanks,
Alex Moreno

Thanks for the ping. I pulled the request ids and traced them to two clusters with higher-than-normal queue times. Early findings:
- There was a kernel patch rolled out in canary on 2026-02-17 that improved latency for <4k sequences but introduced extra per-token memory management overhead for long sequences (8k+).
- Our KV-cache warmup behavior for prefix reuse is suboptimal on long-contxt bursts; we see repeated cold-start computes that push compute >2.5s for 12k-16k requests.
- No obvious network throttling or backend errors — the bulk is compute & queuing.

Immediate mitigations I can push in the next 90 minutes:
1) Roll back the specific kernel change from 02/17 on affected pools (temporary).
2) Enable aggressive KV caching and increase max-batch-size for long-context jobs (config patch attached: kvcache_config_diff.patch).
3) Apply a soft rate-limit for sequences >12k for the next 48h and route overflow to a quantized 16k-compatible variant (rdx-16k-quant) which trades some quality for much lower p99.

Risk note: rollback will re-expose prior p50 improvements for short context. Quantized fallback needs validation for Lexicon's quality bar; Grace can coordinate.

- Dev

Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p95/p99 regressions on our 16k workflows (production)

I ran cluster-level metrics for the last 72h. Observations:
- Two GPU pools (us-west-2-gpu-3 and us-west-2-gpu-7) show sustained higher utilization between 02/17 22:00 and 02/19 00:00 UTC; tail latency correlates with mix of long-seq (>=12k) jobs and some large-batch async jobs.
- Queuing is the primary contributor at p99; compute is second. When long sequences are injected into already-busy pipelines, they push other requests into large queues (thundering effect).

Immediate steps I executed:
- Throttled batch autoscaler on the two pools to favor latency-preserving schedules (reduced max-inflight by 20%).
- Temporarily pinned Lexicon's traffic to a dedicated slot on us-west-2-gpu-11 to isolate their load (rolling for 3 hours).
- Approved Dev's rollback candidate for canary; scheduling a staged rollback starting 02/19 03:00 UTC.

Longer-term proposals for prevention:
1) Long-context traffic shaping: enforce soft rate-limits per-customer for sequences >8k, with configurable SLAs and transparent error codes.
2) Queue-aware routing: route long-seq jobs to pools with explicit headroom and power-profiled kernels.
3) Pre-warm KV-cache for known prefix-heavy customers (Lexicon has predictable document structure).

I've attached a snapshot (latency_dashboard_20260219.png). Grace, can your CS team validate fallback quality for 16k-quant? Hannah — Alex asked about credits/penalties; may need exec sign-off.

-Marcus

Thanks team — I validated the quantized fallback (rdx-16k-quant) against Lexicon's nightly test suite with a 200-sample prompt set. Results:
- ROUGE-style summary delta: average -1.4 points (within Lexicon's acceptable tolerance for background ingestion tasks),
- Occasional tokenization edge-cases on very long legal strings — mitigated by post-token trimming.

I proposed the following customer-facing mitigation plan to Alex in-thread:
1) Short-term (now -> 48h): route >12k sequences to rdx-16k-quant, enable KV-cache warmup and apply soft rate-limit at 10 concurrent long-seq requests.
2) Medium-term (48h -> 2w): staged rollback of kernel on affected pools + validation on canary and production traffic shape rules.
3) Customer remediation: provide Lexicon with a 20% service credit for impacted window and a joint postmortem call next Tues.

Alex — please confirm if the quantized fallback is acceptable for your production ingest path. If yes, we'll turn it on and monitor p95/p99 closely.

- Grace
